Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 9 column B, this return's share of the deductible part of self-employment tax
Fact.Description:
The whole of scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTaxDeduction. On the population this form prints for, the deductible part of the self-employment tax is not split, because the tax it is the deductible part of is not split: Form 8958 says "The deductible portion of the self-employment tax is split only when the self-employment tax is split" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 3, RIGHT column of a two column extraction), and for a MARRIED filer IRC 1402(a)(5)(A) puts the gross income and deductions of a community sole proprietorship on "the spouse carrying on" the trade or business, so the whole of the self-employment tax and the whole of its deductible part sit on the operating spouse's return.
THE STATUTE HAS A THIRD ARM THIS FACT DOES NOT REACH, NAMED RATHER THAN QUOTED AWAY. IRC 1402(a)(5)(A) does not stop at "the spouse carrying on such trade or business" — it continues "or, if such trade or business is jointly operated, treated as the gross income and deductions of each spouse on the basis of their respective distributive share of the gross income and deductions" (26 U.S.C. 1402, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section1402&num=0&edition=2024, LEFT column of a two column extraction). On a JOINTLY OPERATED community sole proprietorship the split is by distributive share, not the whole-on-the-operating-spouse answer this fact gives, and the categorical column C = $0 next to it would not hold either. Nothing in this dictionary models a jointly operated Schedule C or F business today — `jointVenture`, `QJV`, `qualifiedJoint` and `jointlyOperated` are all absent from scheduleC.xml and scheduleSE.xml, and the only "joint venture" fact anywhere in dictionary/ty2025/ is scheduleE:/… for rental property — so nothing computes wrong for any return this dictionary can build today, the same posture as the RDP arm below.
THE RDP CASE IS THE OTHER ANSWER AND IS NOT WIRED. Form 8958 says the section 1402(a)(5) override "does not apply to RDPs. RDPs split self-employment income from sole proprietorships and partnerships for self-employment tax purposes" (same file, lines 152 to 154, RIGHT column), so on an RDP return this cell would be a half. The register's includeWhen is filers:/isCommunityPropertyAllocationReturn, the MFS gate; the RDP twin filers:/isRdpCommunityPropertyAllocationReturn is declared and no fact depends on it, so no RDP return prints this form and this fact is never read on one.
The column A cell prints scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTaxDeduction itself, so column B equals column A here and ../form8958Line9DeductiblePartOfSeTaxColumnCSpouseShare is their difference, which makes the form's footing rule hold by construction rather than by a filer's arithmetic.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 9 column C, the other spouse or RDP share of the deductible part of self-employment tax
Fact.Description: Column A minus column B, which is $0 on every return this form prints for and is written as the difference rather than as a literal zero so that the form's own instruction "Together, columns B and C should equal column A" holds by construction. The reason the answer is zero is on ../form8958Line9DeductiblePartOfSeTaxColumnBThisReturnShare: for a married filer IRC 1402(a)(5)(A) puts the whole of a community sole proprietorship's self-employment tax on the spouse carrying on the business, and Form 8958 splits the deductible part only when the tax is split. A blank cell here invites a filer to halve line 9 by hand and print a Form 8958 that contradicts the Schedule SE in the same package.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 10 column B, this return's share of the self-employment tax
Fact.Description:
The whole of scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTax. Form 8958 states the rule in terms: "Although the self-employment tax rules contain a provision that overrides community income treatment in the case of spouses (section 1402(a)(5))", and then, for a sole proprietorship, "self-employment tax is imposed on the spouse carrying on the trade or business" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f8958.pdf, page 3, RIGHT column of a two column extraction). So on a married separate return the self-employment tax is not allocated at all: the whole of it belongs to the operating spouse, which on this return is this return's taxpayer, because the tax is computed from this return's own Schedule SE.
THE STATUTE HAS A THIRD ARM THIS FACT DOES NOT REACH, NAMED RATHER THAN QUOTED AWAY, exactly as on line 9. IRC 1402(a)(5)(A) continues past "the spouse carrying on such trade or business" to "or, if such trade or business is jointly operated, treated as the gross income and deductions of each spouse on the basis of their respective distributive share of the gross income and deductions" (26 U.S.C. 1402, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section1402&num=0&edition=2024, LEFT column of a two column extraction). A JOINTLY OPERATED community sole proprietorship splits the self-employment tax by distributive share, not whole-on-the-operating-spouse, so this column-B answer and the categorical column C = $0 beside it would not hold there. No jointly operated Schedule C or F business is modelled anywhere in this dictionary today (no `jointVenture`, `QJV`, `qualifiedJoint` or `jointlyOperated` fact in scheduleC.xml or scheduleSE.xml; the only "joint venture" fact in dictionary/ty2025/ is scheduleE:/… for rental property), so nothing computes wrong for any return this dictionary can build today.
THE RDP CASE IS THE OTHER ANSWER AND IS NOT WIRED, exactly as on line 9: RDPs do split self-employment income from sole proprietorships and partnerships for self-employment tax purposes (same file, lines 152 to 154), and no RDP return prints this form today.
Column A prints scheduleSE:/selfEmploymentTax itself and ../form8958Line10SelfEmploymentTaxColumnCSpouseShare is column A minus this fact, so the footing holds by construction.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 10 column C, the other spouse or RDP share of the self-employment tax
Fact.Description: Column A minus column B, which is $0 on every return this form prints for, written as the difference rather than as a literal zero so that "Together, columns B and C should equal column A" holds by construction. The reason is IRC 1402(a)(5)(A), stated on ../form8958Line10SelfEmploymentTaxColumnBThisReturnShare: the self-employment tax on a community sole proprietorship is imposed on the spouse carrying on the business and is not divided.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 11 column B, this return's share of the federal income tax withheld
Fact.Description: Form 1040 line 25d, taxCalculations:/totalWithholding, itself. Six legs of that total are net of the community property allocation: the W-2, 1099-DIV, 1099-R and 1099-MISC withholding totals subtract their allocated halves in their own modules, and the 1099-INT and 1099-G halves ride as adjustments inside the line 25b total. Withholding on income this dictionary does not allocate (Form SSA-1099, W-2G, 1099-PATR, Schedule K-1) stays whole in column B together with the income it was withheld from. Form 1042-S withholding is not allocated: a return with any Form 1042-S is refused (form1042S:/knockoutForm1042SIncomeRoutingUnbuilt), and the community-property half of its withholding is part of the build that refusal stands for. On a return that files, the credit this return claims is this return's share of the withholding, which is what column B prints. Complete wherever line 25d is.

Half the tax withheld on community income leaves this return with the income it was withheld from; withholding on separate income stays whole in column B. $0 on every return that does not allocate community income (filers:/isCommunityPropertyAllocationReturn false), where the form does not print.

Withholding on income this dictionary does not allocate, such as withholding reported on Form SSA-1099, Form W-2G, Form 1099-PATR or Schedule K-1, stays whole in column B with the income it was withheld from.

Fact.Name: Form 8958 line 12, other income — form 1099-misc, column C: the spouse or RDP share
Fact.Description: Column C of the computed Form 8958 line 12 row for other income — form 1099-misc: every Form 1099-MISC community half that leaves this return, summed with cents and rounded once to whole dollars. The halves are the two adjustments that take them off Schedule 1: form1099Misc:/communityPropertyOtherIncomeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded (the box 3, box 8 and box 15 halves off line 8z) and form1099Misc:/communityPropertyPrizeAllocationAdjustmentUnrounded (the prize or award halves off line 8i). Each adjustment is the negated sum of its halves, so this column is their sum with the sign turned back. Reading both adjustments keeps column C the same amounts column B was reduced by, so column A, B plus C, is the whole of the documents' amounts before the allocation, up to the whole-dollar rounding of the two Schedule 1 lines. $0 on every return that does not allocate community income, where each half is $0.
